text: clauses 1, 3, and 4(a), 4(c) (source copies preserve original copyright notices and disclaimers; every otherwise-changed file needs a prominent how-and-when notice; executable-distribution alternatives can require instructions, non-standard names, and separate manual-page documentation, creating a material burden)

text: clause 1; clause 3 opening and alternatives (a)-(d); clause 4 alternatives (a)-(d); clause 5 (copyright/disclaimer preservation, per-file change notices, Freely Available modifications, machine-readable source, Standard-Version executables and acquisition instructions, non-standard executable names/manual pages, fee limits, no own-product advertising, or a separate arrangement with the Copyright Holder); disclose-source and provide-corresponding-source each represent only one alternative, while the vocabulary cannot encode the disjunctions, Standard-Version delivery, naming/manual duties, fee rules, or individualized arrangement, represented by unknown
